chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Rafa'ah ibn Musa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Tawaf around the House and Sa'i, can he voluntarily perform Tawaf before he shortens (his hair/nails)? He (peace be upon him) said: I do not like it.

key_terms.يَسْعَى: performs Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim perform voluntary Tawaf before shortening their hair after Sa'i?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) indicates that performing voluntary Tawaf before the final shortening of hair (Qasr) is disliked (makruh), highlighting the importance of adhering to the specific sequence of Hajr al-Tamattu' rituals. This ruling underscores the scholarly view that the state of Ihram remains active until the completion of Qasr, making premature voluntary acts less optimal. It reflects the precision required in ritual practice to ensure the validity and spiritual integrity of the pilgrimage.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Rafa’at Bin Musa who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who performs Tawaaf by the House, and he performed Sa’ee, can he voluntarily perform the Tawaaf before he has shortened (hair, nails, etc.)?’ Heasws said: Iasws do not like it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Tawaf around the House and Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah; if he can perform an optional Tawaf before Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not admirable to me.’”
